baseline.description: No change: keep the current setup

rule_check.label: Does not shift under 102.20 (DC motor fails) unless de minimis

shown.description: Move the motor stator, the control boards and the electrical apparatus to Canada

verdict.reasoning: In H322161, CBP determined the origin of an actuator assembly classified under heading 8501 (electric motors) was China because the electric motor was manufactured in China, even though the PCBA, cable subassembly, housings, and final assembly occurred in Mexico and gears came from the U.S. The electric motor imparts the essential character of a motor actuator of heading 8501. In Variant B, manufacturing the DC motor, sensor PCBA, and electrical apparatus in Canada (along with final assembly) means the essential character and core electrical components originate in Canada, changing the country of origin from China to Canada.

rule_check.label: Shifts under 102.20 (8501)
rule_check.reason: each foreign material undergoes the change in tariff classification the rule requires, in Canada

shown.description: Move the motor stator, the gearbox assembly, the screw drive, the control boards and the electrical apparatus to Canada

verdict.reasoning: In H322161, CBP held that the country of origin of an actuator assembly classified under heading 8501 was determined by the country of origin of the electric motor, even where the PCBA, housing, and cable subassemblies were manufactured and assembled with gears in another country. In Variant A, the DC motor and all other components are made in China, making China the origin. In Variant B, the DC motor, gearbox assembly, screw drive, sensor PCBA, and electrical apparatus are all produced in Canada (only the housings are from China), shifting the essential character and origin to Canada.

rule_check.label: Shifts under 102.20 (8501)

others.description: Move the motor stator to Canada

verdict.reasoning: The finished DC motor actuator is classified in heading 8501 as an electric motor (consistent with CBP classification of motorized actuators in N342620). In Variant A, all major components including the DC motor are made in China and merely assembled in Canada, giving Chinese origin. In Variant B, the DC motor itself (also heading 8501, which imparts the essential character of a motor/actuator of 8501) is manufactured in-house in Canada and combined there with the Chinese gearbox, screw drive, housing, and PCBA. Analogous to N346297 (where manufacturing the core electric motor subassembly in the assembly country alongside a Chinese gearbox conferred origin), producing the DC motor in Canada changes the origin to Canada.

others.description: Move the motor stator, the gearbox assembly and the screw drive to Canada

verdict.reasoning: In Variant A, all major components of the DC motor actuator (classified in heading 8501)—including the DC motor, gearbox assembly, and screw drive—are produced in China and merely assembled in Canada, resulting in Chinese origin. In Variant B, the core functional components that impart the essential character of the actuator (the 12 VDC brushed motor, gearbox assembly, and screw drive) are manufactured in-house in Canada and assembled there with Chinese housings, sensor PCBA, and electrical apparatus. Because the motor and drive mechanism are produced in Canada, the country of origin shifts to Canada.

others.description: Move the motor stator and the housing to Canada

verdict.reasoning: In Variant A, all components (DC motor, gearbox, screw drive, housings, PCBA, electrical apparatus) are made in China and undergo simple assembly in Canada, conferring Chinese origin. In Variant B, production of the DC motor (the core subassembly imparting the essential character of the heading 8501 motor actuator) and the housings moves to Canada, while the gearbox, screw drive, and PCBA remain Chinese. As in N346297 (where an electric winch assembled in Thailand from a Chinese gearbox and a Thai-produced electric motor and drum was held to originate in Thailand), manufacturing the electric motor in Canada shifts origin to Canada.

draft.plan: Move the motor stator, the control boards and the electrical apparatus to Canada
draft.question:
What is the country of origin of DC motor actuator, produced as described above, under the Part 102 rules of origin (the general rules of 19 C.F.R. § 102.11, applied in order, with the tariff shifts of § 102.20), for purposes of country of origin marking (19 C.F.R. § 102.0)?

This request concerns the origin of the merchandise for marking under the Part 102 rules only. It does not ask CBP to decide the country of origin for Section 301 duties, which is a separate question, and the requester does not contend that marking origin settles it.
draft.tariff_shift: Tariff-shift check (19 C.F.R. § 102.20): applied to the component codes in the bill of materials, with the good finished in Canada, the rule gives Canada (19 C.F.R. § 102.11(a)(3); 19 C.F.R. § 102.20(o), 8501). [CONFIRM WITH COUNSEL]
notes: Asked under the Part 102 rules (19 C.F.R. § 102.11) for marking because the prediction behind the requester's position was made under that regime. Marking origin does not settle the separate Section 301 question; this draft does not ask it. Confirm that regime applies.
